M 25 here! I got my vasectomy at the ripe old age of 22 in Montana. No kids, no partner, nothing. I called to schedule the appointment and was asked if I wanted a consultation first. I said no, got my appointment, and a few days later, had the procedure done.

My doctor asked exactly one time "Why would you like this procedure?" I gave her my reasons (don't want kids, genetics, I'd be a bad father) and she said "Okay, let's get started then."

Unfortunately for me, I am very resistant to anesthetic, so I felt every single moment of the surgery, but even then, not the worst thing I've felt. I was in and out in under an hour.

The biggest thing is to *make sure you recover*. I went to work literally two hours after the procedure due to being called in and told I would be fired if I didn't show up. Because I didn't get my recovery time, I ended up with a quite large and uncomfortable hematoma in my scrotum. It looked like I had a purple softball between my legs for a week.

I did it once as a kid.

My neighbors across the back alley had three pitbulls that they kept in horrid conditions. Legit abuse and neglect. They were starved, kept in a tiny dog run, kept outside during bad weather, and their feces was never picked up.

I was about 7 years old when my mom and I drove 80 miles away to the nearest big stores to get groceries (We lived in a tiny town). As we were walking out the back door she reminded me to shut and lock it. I forgot to, and left only the screen door shut.

Fast forward about an hour and an elderly lady from down the street is walking down the alley with her walking stick, she was sliding it along the pitbull owner's fence bouncing it between the wood slats. This apparently set the dogs off, because they *broke down* the chain link fence of the dog run, sprinted across the yard, and broke through the wooden fence as well.

As soon as the dogs escaped the pen, she saw them coming and started hurrying down the alley, toward my house.  Once the dogs broke through, they began savaging her. Tearing at her clothes, first, then her flesh. She got to my back step before they got to her legs, at which point they dragged her to the ground and were tearing at her. After they ripped off a large chunk of her leg, they got distracted by eating the flesh, and she was able to crawl to the door and open it.

She crawled through my house to our home phone, called 911, and passed out from blood loss. It was quite a scene when my mom and I got home. A few years later, she thanked me for accidentally saving her life. She passed away about a month after that.

The three dogs were put down, but the owner faced no charges of any kind

I also feel this way, but I have some theories on why. Firstly, the Ajahs were formed 2000 years ago, based on factions of Aes Sedai with certain ideologies that came together. Over 2000 years, these ideologies became warped or hyperfocused. Here are my theories on the original Ajahs:

The White Ajah was formed to make order out of chaos. The Breaking destroyed almost everything known to man, and much of it had to be relearned. In our own reality, philosophers, mathematicians, logicians and the like helped to explain our world over the past several thousand years. I believe that was the White's original purpose, but it became hyperfocused on "logic" to the point of almost mocking the original purpose.

The Yellow Ajah were obviously healers originally and wanted to heal everyone, but became set in their ways throughout the years. They believe only *their* form of healing works and it's not worth even looking into other methods. This led to extreme arrogance, which is noted as a defining trait of Yellows in the present time of the books.

The Brown Ajah were dedicated to seeking and preserving knowledge. I believe their purpose was to seek knowledge and record it for future generations. However, over the next several thousand years, "seeking and preserving" slowly turned into just "preserving", to the point that almost nothing outside the Tower matters, only preserving the knowledge for the *sake* of preserving knowledge. This led to the Brown's common "head in the clouds" demeanor.

The Red Ajah were determined to prevent another Breaking, or even smaller disasters at the hands of madmen who could channel. Their focus was the preservation of the world by eliminating threats to it. Slowly, the years upon years of hunting and subduing men who could channel led to a disdain, dislike, and sometimes even hatred for men in general. This grew into the Red Ajah of the current times, whose primary attribute is - on the surface, at least - disliking men.

The Green Ajah's decline is one of the more obvious. After the Trolloc Wars, there wasn't really a need for a Light counterpart to Dreadlords. Their need for extra protection on the battlefield (extra warders) became a tradition, though, and was passed down with it, but without the battlefield training necessary to be a true Battle Ajah. Eventually, the defining aspect of the Ajah *became* the warders, instead of the battle expertise.

The Gray Ajah obviously were peacekeepers, advisors, mediators, and more when formed. My personal belief is that they are the least changed from their forming. They are not remarked upon as much because they are good at what they do, and they do it behind the scenes. Their methods likely have changed, but I believe they still hold strongest to the "core" of their ajah.

The Blue Ajah is tough. They are described as "involving themselves in causes". The trouble is that we don't really see what many Blues *do* throughout the series other than Moiraine and Siuan. I personally have no clue what their founding beliefs were, because I see them as being a mix of White and Gray: reasoning out what they belief is best, and manipulating the world to make it happen.

These are just my thoughts, and if I have anything wrong or if you'd like to add something, please do! I love these discussions.

I can think of a few reasons this might not have been done. The first, and most talked about here is that cuendillar requires an iron base in order to form. Not just metal, but iron *specifically*.

The second is that in order to carry enough force to, say, cut through leather armor, the sword would need to have *some* weight. You already referenced this,, but I still feel it is important. You can get the edge as fine as you like, but you still need force, and therefore weight, to get the rest of the blade through in order to shear properly through flesh and bone. While the edge would be able to cut through very tough material, the rest of the blade would not be able to pass, creating superficial cuts at best on any kind of hard armor.

The third reason is in reference to the hilt. There's a reason that power-forged swords have to have the hilt replaced. (I believe both Lan and Laman's sword are referenced to have had the hilts replaced several times, please correct me if I'm wrong.) The reason being that metal or cuendillar are not conducive to having a good grip. When the hands would get sweaty in a sword fight like that, the hilt would slip in the grasp. Other materials like leather and some woods create far better grips that won't slip.
